rows.title: API Design and Integration in a Microservices Environment
rows.venue: International Journal for Research Publication and Seminars
rows.abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving software landscape, microservices have emerged as a robust architectural approach that promotes scalability, agility, and resilience. This paper examines the critical role of API design and integration within a microservices environment, focusing on how well-architected APIs can streamline communication among discrete services. It delves into the principles of crafting RESTful APIs that adhere to industry best practices while also exploring alternative paradigms like GraphQL and gRPC. rows.title: From Automation to Intelligence: Revolutionizing Microservices and API Testing with AI
rows.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
rows.abstract: The shift to Microservices architecture and Application Programming Interface (API) - first development has transformed the landscape of software engineering, empowering development teams to create highly scalable, modular systems with agile, independent service deployment. However, the complexities of distributed architectures present unique challenges that traditional testing methodologies are often ill-equipped to address. rows.title: NODE.JS PROJECT ARCHITECTURE WITH SHARED DEPENDENCIES FOR MICROSERVICES
rows.abstract: Microservices is an architectural style in software development that involves constructing a big solution using small, self-contained services. A set of services are connected via well-defined APIs and work together like a coherent system. The application of microservices architecture spans a wide range of domains, e.g., healthcare, finance, government, military, gaming, and entertainment. This article analyzes existing project architecture approaches for Node.js, and improves scalable project architecture for Node.js using shared dependencies. rows.venue: International journal of computer science and applications
rows.abstract: This study aims to check suitable software testing tools for testing microservices architectures, which have become increasingly popular in software development due to their advantages.However, testing microservices architectures poses unique challenges, and the e effectiveness of testing tools is investigated.The study will review the literature and conduct experiments using common testing tools on a microservicesbased application to evaluate their effectiveness in detecting bugs, vulnerabilities, and performance issues.The study will us a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods t

rows.title: Performance Evaluation of RESTful APIs in Microservices-Based Enterprise Application Using Load Testing Techniques
rows.venue: Best Journal of Innovation in Science Research and Development
rows.authors: Yogesh Sonvane; Nikita Bhoyar; Prajwesh Walekar
rows.abstract: Modern enterprise systems are increasingly designed using microservices architecture, where RESTful APIs serve as the primary communication mechanism between distributed services. Ensuring optimal API performance is essential for maintaining system scalability, responsiveness, and reliability. However, traditional load testing techniques rely on static workloads and fail to capture real-world traffic variability and inter-service dependencies. This paper presents an adaptive load testing framework for evaluating RESTful API performance in microservices-based enterprise applications. The propos

rows.title: Microservices for multimedia
rows.authors: Frank San Miguel; Naveen Mareddy; Anush Krishna Moorthy; Xiaomei Liu
rows.abstract: Netflix has been one of the pioneers that has driven the industry adoption of a new paradigm of system architecture referred to as "microservices". Microservices, or more accurately, microservice architecture refers to an architecture where applications are modeled as a collection of services which are: highly maintainable and independently testable, loosely coupled, independently deployable and organized around business capabilities. rows.title: Handling Communication via APIs for Microservices
rows.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering: New Ideas and Emerging Results (ICSE-NIER)
rows.authors: Vini Kanvar; Ridhi Jain; Srikanth Tamilselvam
rows.abstract: Enterprises in their journey to the cloud, want to decompose their monolith applications into microservices to maximize cloud benefits. Current research focuses a lot on how to partition the monolith into smaller clusters that perform well across standard metrics like coupling, cohesion etc. However, there is little research done on taking the partitions, identifying their dependencies between the microservices, exploring ways to further reduce the dependencies, and making appropriate code changes to enable robust communication without changing the application behaviour.In this work, we discus

rows.title: Microservices Architecture
rows.venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
rows.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of microservices architecture, focusing on its implementation.We discuss the core principles, key components, deployment considerations, challenges, and best practices for building robust and scalable microservices-based applications with C#.The paper emphasizes the benefits of adopting microservices, such as improved scalability, agility, and maintainability, while also addressing common challenges like distributed system complexity and data management.Specific examples and code snippets illustrate the practical aspects of implementing microservice

rows.title: Microservice API Evolution in Practice: A Study on Strategies and Challenges
rows.authors: Alexander Lercher; Johann Glock; Christian Macho; Martin Pinzger
rows.abstract: Nowadays, many companies design and develop their software systems as a set of loosely coupled microservices that communicate via their Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). While the loose coupling improves maintainability, scalability, and fault tolerance, it poses new challenges to the API evolution process. Related works identified communication and integration as major API evolution challenges but did not provide the underlying reasons and research directions to mitigate them. rows.title: Inferring Relations Among Test Programs in Microservices Applications
rows.venue: IEEE International Conference on Service-Oriented System Engineering (SOSE)
rows.authors: Emanuele De Angelis; Guglielmo De Angelis; Alessandro Pellegrini; Maurizio Proietti
rows.abstract: The emergence of the microservices-oriented architectural style calls for novel methodologies and technological frameworks that support the design, development, and main-tainance of applications structured according to this new style. In this paper, we consider the issue of designing suitable strategies for the governance and the automation of testing activities within the microservices paradigm. We focus on the problem of discovering relations between test programs that help avoiding to re-run all the available test suites each time one of its constituents evolves. rows.title: Theoretical Frameworks for API-First and Shift-Left Quality Engineering in Microservices Architectures
rows.venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
rows.abstract: Microservices architectures have shifted the model of how quality is assured. Specifically: end-to-end screening strategies used in monolithic architectures are not viable because UI centric approaches have delays in defect discovery; and resolving architectural defects post integration requires orders of magnitude more effort than resolving defects found at the level of service contracts. rows.title: MIRAGE: Online LLM Simulation for Microservice Dependency Testing
rows.abstract: Existing approaches to microservice dependency simulation--record-replay, pattern-mining, and specification-driven stubs--generate static artifacts before test execution. These artifacts can only reproduce behaviors encoded at generation time; on error-handling and code-reasoning scenarios, which are underrepresented in typical trace corpora, record-replay achieves 0% and 12% fidelity in our evaluation. rows.title: A microservice regression testing selection approach based on belief propagation
rows.venue: Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications
rows.authors: Li-zhe Chen; Ji Tao Wu; Haiyan Yang; Kui Zhang
rows.abstract: Abstract Regression testing is required in each iteration of microservice systems. Regression testing selection, which reduces testing costs by selecting a subset from the original test cases, is one of the main techniques to optimize regression testing.
